newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Costello says "living wage" would cost jobs.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Costello says "living wage" would cost jobs.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Friday that Australia could not afford the "living wage" claim proposed by the Australian Council of Trade Unions (ACTU).
"Australia cannot afford the ACTU's living wage claim," Costello said.
"Our argument will be that granting the ACTU's living wage claim will probably create the loss of 400,000 jobs," he added.

The ACTU, Australia's peak union body, has proposed to the Industrial Relations Commission that all workers not covered by workplace deals get a 8.75 percent increase in award rates and three A$20 a week safety net adjustments over three years.
The government is proposing a A$24 per week wage rise for lower paid workers spread over three years.
Costello was speaking at a business luncheon.
